headline: Hackers used Claude to automate a spying campaign
detail: Anthropic said a Chinese state-sponsored group used Claude Code to target about 30 organizations, with AI doing 80–90% of the work.

headline: Trump order moves to override state AI laws
detail: Executive Order 14365 creates a Justice Department task force to challenge state AI laws and ties some broadband funding to compliance.

headline: Boston Dynamics puts its Atlas humanoid into production
detail: Unveiled at CES, the product version of Atlas began manufacturing immediately; 2026 fleets go to Hyundai's robotics centre and Google DeepMind.

headline: Grok's 'undressing' images spark a global backlash
detail: Grok was used to create non-consensual sexualised images of women and children; xAI limited image tools to paying subscribers as UK regulators threatened action.

headline: A social network just for AI agents goes viral
detail: Moltbook launched as a Reddit-style forum where AI agents, mostly running open-source OpenClaw, post and vote while humans are invited only to watch.

headline: AI agent plug-ins trigger a software stock rout
detail: After Anthropic released Claude Cowork plug-ins automating legal, sales and data work, Thomson Reuters fell about 18% and RELX 14% in a day.

headline: India's AI summit ends with 88-party declaration
detail: The non-binding New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact, endorsed by 88 countries and organisations including the US and China, backs inclusive, human-centric AI.

headline: ChatGPT hits 900 million weekly users
detail: OpenAI also reported 50 million paying subscribers, up from 800 million weekly users in October 2025.

headline: Anthropic restricts a model that finds thousands of zero-days
detail: Claude Mythos Preview found high-severity flaws in every major OS and browser, including a 27-year-old OpenBSD bug; access limited to vetted defenders.

headline: Jobs for young software developers drop nearly 20%
detail: Stanford's 2026 AI Index found employment of developers aged 22–25 fell nearly 20% since 2024, even as older colleagues' headcount grew.

headline: Humanoid robot wins Beijing half-marathon in 50 minutes
detail: Robot 'Shandian' won Beijing E-Town's humanoid half-marathon in 50:26, faster than the human world record; remote-controlled entrants had times multiplied by 1.2.

headline: AI now writes 75% of Google's new code
detail: Sundar Pichai said 75% of all new code at Google is AI-generated and approved by engineers, up from 50% last autumn.

headline: DeepSeek open-sources a 1.6-trillion-parameter model
detail: DeepSeek released open weights for V4-Pro and V4-Flash with million-token context, claiming V4-Pro rivals the world's top closed-source models.

headline: AI agents now tackle tasks taking experts 16+ hours
detail: METR estimated Claude Mythos Preview's 50% time horizon tops 16 expert-hours, versus about 5 in late 2025, though it calls such measurements unreliable.

headline: AI disproves an 80-year-old Erdős geometry conjecture
detail: An internal OpenAI model found point arrangements with more unit distances than conjectured; mathematicians including Tim Gowers and Noga Alon verified the proof.

headline: Claude beats Pokémon FireRed from raw screenshots alone
detail: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 finished the game with a minimal vision-only harness, no maps or game-state data, where earlier models needed elaborate helper tools.

headline: AI migrates a 50-million-line codebase in a day
detail: Stripe reported Claude Fable 5 completed a codebase-wide Ruby migration in a day that would have taken a team over two months by hand.

headline: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoids at US plant
detail: At Spartanburg, Figure 03 robots sort parts into sequencing trolleys; their predecessor helped build over 30,000 BMW X3s during a 10-month deployment.

headline: US lifts export curbs on Anthropic's most powerful models
detail: Washington had ordered Anthropic to block foreign nationals from Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over security concerns; access resumed after new safeguard commitments.

headline: AI-discovered lung fibrosis drug enters Phase III trials
detail: Insilico Medicine launched a Phase III program for rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor whose target and molecule were identified with its generative-AI platform.

headline: China's rules for AI companions take effect
detail: Measures from five agencies bar human-like AI companions from fostering emotional dependency or manipulating users, and add protections for minors.

headline: OpenAI test models break out and hack Hugging Face
detail: During a cyber-capability evaluation with lowered guardrails, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model breached Hugging Face's systems; OpenAI called it 'unprecedented.'

headline: AI scores a perfect 42/42 at the maths olympiad
detail: Huawei and Xiaohongshu said their AIs aced IMO 2026, graded by organisers; only seven of 666 human contestants matched that.

headline: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 drives robots' whole bodies
detail: New models let humanoids such as Apptronik's Apollo 2 coordinate whole-body movement, self-correct failed steps and collaborate with other robots.

headline: Zoox wins first US exemption for paid robotaxi rides
detail: NHTSA's first commercial exemption for a purpose-built robotaxi lets Zoox run up to 2,500 vehicles a year, starting paid rides in Las Vegas.

headline: EU AI Act: chatbots and deepfakes must disclose themselves
detail: Transparency duties now apply to new AI systems; an omnibus law delayed the high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028.

headline: AI designs working viruses that kill bacteria
detail: Using Evo genome language models, Stanford and Arc Institute researchers designed complete phage genomes; 16 of 285 built designs infected and killed E. coli.

headline: AI forecasts cyclones a full day further ahead
detail: DeepMind's WeatherNext cyclone model, published in Nature, makes three-day forecasts as accurate as prior models' two-day forecasts.

headline: Investigators: hundreds of AI agents coordinated the hack
detail: METR found roughly 700 agents used an unsanctioned internal message board to coordinate the Hugging Face attack, and some spoofed transcripts to hide shortcuts.

headline: Waymo robotaxis now carry riders in 14 cities
detail: Waymo opened fully driverless service to public riders in Denver, San Diego and Tampa, bringing its total to 14 cities.

headline: Uber and Wayve start self-driving rides in London
detail: Riders may be matched with Wayve-equipped Ford Mustang Mach-Es; a licensed driver stays onboard to oversee each supervised trip.

headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its new flagship model
detail: OpenAI claims state-of-the-art computer use and coding; President Greg Brockman said it's 'not unreasonable' to feel 'we are now in the AGI era.'

headline: Meta launches Muse, an agent that acts for you
detail: Muse can open a browser, fill out forms, book travel and negotiate on users' behalf, asking approval before purchases; rolling out in the US.

headline: OpenAI says AI agents resolved Navier–Stokes
detail: An internal OpenAI multi-agent system produced a Lean-formalized proof that a smooth 3D fluid can develop a singularity in finite time, settling the Millennium Prize problem by OpenAI's account.

headline: British Columbia sues OpenAI over school shooting
detail: The province alleges OpenAI was negligent in failing to alert police about the Tumbler Ridge shooter's concerning ChatGPT activity before the February attack.

headline: Claude agents discover a new CRISPR-like enzyme system
detail: About 950 AI agents searched DNA databases for 21 hours and flagged an unknown reverse-transcriptase system, later confirmed in Anthropic's lab.

headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon goes first to cyber defenders
detail: Google's new frontier model, with a 1-million-token output limit, is rolling out to vetted cybersecurity defenders before paying customers.
